questions.question: In which of the following battles did Alexander the Great defeat Porus of Paurava in 326 BC?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Hydaspes (326 BC): Battle of Hydaspes
  • History: Fought on the banks of the Jhelum River; Alexander defeated King Porus but was impressed by his bravery.

questions.question: ho was the founder of Brahmo Samaj in 1828, at Calcutta?
questions.solution:
• Brahmo Samaj (1828): Raja Ram Mohan Roy
  • Focus: It aimed at the worship of the Eternal God and opposed idol worship and Sati.

questions.question: hich of the following dynasties ruled over Delhi just after the Sayyid dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Post-Sayyid Dynasty: Lodi dynasty
  • Chronology: Bahlul Lodi established the first Afghan dynasty in Delhi after the fall of the Sayyids.

questions.question: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river Hugli in ______.
questions.solution:
• Hugli Factory (1651): 1651
  • Trade: This was the first English base in Bengal, allowing them to trade and set up warehouses.

questions.question: Dhamek stupa is one of the most prominent Buddhist structures in India. It is situated in the ______ district of Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
• Dhamek Stupa: Varanasi
  • Significance: Located at Sarnath, it marks the spot where Buddha gave his first sermon.

questions.question: Which of the following titles was held by Samudragupta, a ruler of the Gupta Dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Kaviraja Title: Samudragupta
  • Detail: He was a great patron of art and music, often depicted on coins playing the Veena.

questions.question: ho led the Battle of Plassey on behalf of the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Plassey Leader: Robert Clive
  • 1757: His victory against Siraj-ud-Daulah established the Company's political footprint.

questions.question: abur, the first Mughal emperor, succeeded to the throne of Ferghana in 1494 when he was only ______ years old.
questions.solution:
• Babur's Accession (1494): 12 years old
  • Fact: He inherited the throne of Ferghana (modern Uzbekistan) at a very young age.

questions.question: As per the Rigvedic or Early Vedic Period (1500-1000 BC), who among the following was a River Goddess?
questions.solution:
• Rigvedic River Goddess: Sindhu
  • Note: While Agni (Fire) and Usha (Dawn) were important, Sindhu (Indus) was revered as a major river deity.

questions.question: Dholavira, which was the ancient Harappan site was divided into ______ parts.
questions.solution:
• Dholavira Structure: Three parts
  • Architecture: Unlike most Harappan cities (2 parts), Dholavira had a Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town.

questions.question: The Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar died in ______.
questions.solution:
• Bahadur Shah Zafar Death: 1862
  • Exile: The last Mughal Emperor died in Rangoon, Burma, after being deposed by the British.

questions.question: ho was the Governor-General of India when the permanent settlement was introduced in 1793?
questions.solution:
• Permanent Settlement (1793): Charles Cornwallis
  • Revenue: This system fixed the land revenue for Zamindars in Bengal and Bihar permanently.

questions.question: Banabhatta was the court poet of ______.
questions.solution:
• Banabhatta's Patron: Harshavardhana
  • Literature: He wrote the 'Harshacharita' and 'Kadambari' in Sanskrit.

questions.question: ehrunnisa married Emperor Jahangir in ______.
questions.solution:
• Mehrunnisa (Nur Jahan): 1611
  • Note: She became the power behind the throne during Jahangir's later reign.

questions.question: All of the following are freedom fighters of India who were hanged to death on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore conspiracy case, EXCEPT _________.
questions.solution:
• Lahore Conspiracy Case: Mahatma Gandhi (Not Hanged)
  • Martyrs: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were the three executed on 23 March 1931.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter abolished the Zamindari System in Uttar Pradesh and was elected as the Home Minister in 1955?
questions.solution:
• Govind Ballabh Pant: Govind Ballabh Pant
  • Achievement: He was a key figure in the abolition of the Zamindari system and later served as India's Home Minister.
